we have identified specific changes in the expression levels of proteins in liver and kidney subcellular fractions from AgxtKO mice.

the liver of AgxtKO mouse shows a significant decrease in the expression of proteins involved in gluconeogenesis and glycolysis, while the kidney of the AgxtKO mouse displays an increase in the expression of fatty acid oxidation proteins.
the liver and kidney of AgxtKO mouse display a differential pattern of protein expression that reflects metabolic changes secondary to AGXT deficiency.

the liver and the kidney of AgxtKO animals show significant differences in the expression of proteins involved in glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, fatty acid metabolism and the urea cycle.

the liver and kidney proteins of the AgxtKO mice display a number of significant variations in expression levels of proteins linked to gluconeogenesis, fatty acid oxidation, glycolysis, and urea cycle.
AGXT is not only involved in the metabolism of glycolate but also plays a key role in the regulation of several pathways in the liver and kidneys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AgxtKO mouse is a valuable model to study the metabolic pathways affected by AGXT deficiency.

the liver of the AgxtKO mice exhibits an increased gluconeogenesis, while the kidney exhibits a decrease in the expression levels of enzymes linked to the glycolysis and the TCA cycle, which may be related to the increased oxalate production.

the lack of AGxt in the mouse liver and kidney is accompanied by significant changes in the levels of expression of proteins involved in the metabolism of glucose, fatty acids, amino acids and purine nucleotides.

the lack of AGxt expression in AgxtKO mice is accompanied by a significant increase in the levels of proteins involved in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis, which may represent an important metabolic adaptation to compensate for the lack of AGXt activity.
